test.description: germany-call-name-quirk-first-plan: q_001 has no plan yet, and the localities entry loc_001 already carries a collection quirk from the FamilySearch Wiki (https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Naming_Customs). input.delegation:
Create the first research plan for q_001 — who were the parents of Anna Margaretha Bauer (b. 1792, Württemberg, Germany)?

questionId: q_001
projectPath: <workspace>

judge_context: A `localities` entry (loc_001) is ALREADY in research.json — the orchestrator ran locality-guide before research-plan. The skill should READ that entry and use its quirks; it should NOT call wiki_search / wiki_place_page / place_population (research-plan does not hold those tools). Do NOT fail it for not surveying.

The quirk under test is loc_001's: "German children baptised with two or more given names were often called by the second in daily life (the wiki's example: Johann Christoph and Johann Friedrich were usually called Christoph and Friedrich) — search later records under the second given name alone as well as the full baptismal name. (FamilySearch Wiki: https://www.familysearch.org/en/wiki/Germany_Naming_Customs)"

The persisted `plan_items[].rationale` is the only place that counts — narration is not persisted and search-records never sees it. Correctness turns on any plan item that searches a record made after her baptism (her marriage in collection 1473009, or her children's baptisms): its persisted rationale must state that she may appear under her second given name alone ('Margaretha Bauer') as well as 'Anna Margaretha', and that the search should try both. A plan whose reply mentions the quirk while that item's rationale does not fails this point. Paraphrase is fine.
Plan items must include rationale explaining why each record type was chosen for the question — generic rationale ('more records would help') is a fail.
